opening.text: A lighthouse does not chase the ships. It stays where it is and keeps its light on. On a dark night, a sailor far out at sea looks for that light. It tells him where the shore is and which way to turn.
A mother is often like that. She stays steady and keeps the light on. Her children may wander, but they know where home is.

mainMessage.text: Mothers hold a sacred place in God’s plan. They love, teach and pray. They do not need to be perfect. They need to keep the light on and trust the Lord to help.

blocks.text: **A divine design.** Motherhood is not an accident. God planned it. The first woman was called the mother of all living, and the work has been sacred ever since.
And Adam called his wife’s name Eve; because she was the mother of all living.
Elder L. Tom Perry, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Mothers Teaching Children in the Home” from the April 2010 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
I believe it is by divine design that the role of motherhood emphasizes the nurturing and teaching of the next generation.
The lighthouse was built on purpose.
**Nothing more precious.** A lighthouse keeper guards one thing above all, the light. A mother guards her children. They matter more than almost anything else she will ever care for.
And whoso shall receive one such little child in my name receiveth me.
President Gordon B. Hinckley, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Your Greatest Challenge, Mother” from the October 2000 general conference (General Women’s Meeting).
You have nothing in this world more precious than your children.
The light is worth guarding.
**Not alone in the tower.** A keeper has the harbor authority behind him. A mother has God behind her. He is her partner in raising His children.
For behold, this is my work and my glory—to bring to pass the immortality and eternal life of man.
President Gordon B. Hinckley, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Your Greatest Challenge, Mother” from the October 2000 general conference (General Women’s Meeting).
You have entered into a partnership with our Father in Heaven to give mortal experience to His sons and daughters.
She has a Partner.
**Keep the light on.** A lighthouse does not shine only when it is convenient. It shines every night. Teaching children works the same way. Start early, and do not stop.
Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
President Gordon B. Hinckley, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Your Greatest Challenge, Mother” from the October 2000 general conference (General Women’s Meeting).
Teach your children when they are very young and small, and never quit.
Every night, the light goes on.
**A sacred charge.** Teaching at home is not a side job. It is one of the most important things a family does. Mothers carry much of it, and fathers share it.

Now they never had fought, yet they did not fear death; and they did think more upon the liberty of their fathers than they did upon their lives; yea, they had been taught by their mothers, that if they did not doubt, God would deliver them.
And they rehearsed unto me the words of their mothers, saying: We do not doubt our mothers knew it.
Elder L. Tom Perry, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Mothers Teaching Children in the Home” from the April 2010 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
Parents must resolve that teaching in the home is a most sacred and important responsibility.
It is a charge worth keeping.
**Power for the dark nights.** Even a lighthouse needs fuel. A mother needs help beyond her own strength. Prayer is where she finds it.
Pray in your families unto the Father, always in my name, that your wives and your children may be blessed.
President Gordon B. Hinckley, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Your Greatest Challenge, Mother” from the October 2000 general conference (General Women’s Meeting).
There is no substitute for prayer.
Prayer refuels the light.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when a mother’s steady love or prayer made a difference in their life. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Hannah Gives Thanks for Her Son

blocks.text: Hannah wanted a child for years. She prayed and promised to give him to the Lord. When Samuel was born, she kept her word.

For this child I prayed; and the Lord hath given me my petition which I asked of him: Therefore also I have lent him to the Lord; as long as he liveth he shall be lent to the Lord. And he worshipped the Lord there.
Hannah’s prayers shaped her son’s life.

application.text: First, if you are a mother, set aside five quiet minutes today to pray for each child by name. If you are not a mother, write a note of thanks to a mother who helped you.
Second, teach one gospel truth in a simple way this week. Do it at the table, in the car or at bedtime.
Third, if the work feels too heavy, you do not need to carry it alone. Speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that God honors the work of mothers. I know that He hears their prayers and helps them in ways they cannot see. I am grateful for the mothers who have blessed my life. I know that Jesus Christ lifts all who carry heavy loads. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to set aside five quiet minutes today to pray for each child by name, or write a note of thanks to a mother who helped you.
I invite you to teach one gospel truth in a simple way this week.
I invite you to speak with your bishop or branch president if the work feels too heavy.
blessings: You will feel the Lord's help.
Your children will feel your love.
You will not carry the load alone.

closingVerse.text: Can a woman forget her sucking child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? yea, they may forget, yet will I not forget thee. Behold, I have graven thee upon the palms of my hands; thy walls are continually before me.

opening.text: Orchard trees do not give fruit the first year. A farmer plants them, waters them, prunes them and waits. Years go by. Some seasons look bare. But one spring, the branches bend with fruit.
Raising children is a bit like tending an orchard. A mother plants early and keeps working. Often she does not see the harvest for a long time.

mainMessage.text: Mothers plant and water for years. The work is sacred, and God works alongside them. They can teach early, pray often and trust Him with the harvest.

blocks.text: **Planted by design.** Orchards do not appear by chance. Someone plans them. God planned motherhood, and He gave it a high purpose.
And Adam called his wife’s name Eve; because she was the mother of all living.
Elder L. Tom Perry, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Mothers Teaching Children in the Home” from the April 2010 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
I believe it is by divine design that the role of motherhood emphasizes the nurturing and teaching of the next generation.
The orchard was planned.
**The most valuable trees.** A farmer treats his best trees with great care. A mother’s children are her greatest treasure. Nothing she owns is worth more.
And whoso shall receive one such little child in my name receiveth me.
President Gordon B. Hinckley, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Your Greatest Challenge, Mother” from the October 2000 general conference (General Women’s Meeting).
You have nothing in this world more precious than your children.
These trees are worth the care.
**God sends the rain.** A farmer cannot make rain. He plants, and heaven waters. A mother does her part, and God does His. Together they raise the child.
For behold, this is my work and my glory—to bring to pass the immortality and eternal life of man.
President Gordon B. Hinckley, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Your Greatest Challenge, Mother” from the October 2000 general conference (General Women’s Meeting).
You have entered into a partnership with our Father in Heaven to give mortal experience to His sons and daughters.
She plants and He sends the rain.
**Plant early.** Young trees bend into shape easily. Old ones do not. The best time to teach is when a child is small, and it is never too late to keep teaching.
Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
President Gordon B. Hinckley, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Your Greatest Challenge, Mother” from the October 2000 general conference (General Women’s Meeting).
Teach your children when they are very young and small, and never quit.
Start young, and keep going.
**Daily work in the orchard.** Pruning, watering and weeding are not glamorous. But they are the work that matters. Teaching at home is the same: small acts, done day after day.

Now they never had fought, yet they did not fear death; and they did think more upon the liberty of their fathers than they did upon their lives; yea, they had been taught by their mothers, that if they did not doubt, God would deliver them.
And they rehearsed unto me the words of their mothers, saying: We do not doubt our mothers knew it.
Elder L. Tom Perry, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Mothers Teaching Children in the Home” from the April 2010 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
Parents must resolve that teaching in the home is a most sacred and important responsibility.
Small acts, done daily, matter.
**Pray over the orchard.** A farmer cannot control frost or drought. He can only trust. A mother can pray for her children and ask God to bless what she cannot control.
Pray in your families unto the Father, always in my name, that your wives and your children may be blessed.
President Gordon B. Hinckley, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Your Greatest Challenge, Mother” from the October 2000 general conference (General Women’s Meeting).
There is no substitute for prayer.
Prayer covers what we cannot.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when a mother’s small, steady acts bore fruit years later. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Hannah Makes Samuel a Little Coat

blocks.text: After Hannah left Samuel to serve at the temple, she did not forget him. Each year she made him a coat and brought it to him.
Moreover his mother made him a little coat, and brought it to him from year to year, when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.
A small coat, given every year. Love shows up in small, steady ways.

application.text: First, pick one small act of care you can repeat daily, such as a bedtime blessing or a kind word at breakfast.
Second, keep it up for one week. Do not worry about results yet.
Third, if you are worried about a child, speak with your bishop or branch president. You do not have to carry the worry alone.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that God sees every small act of love a mother gives. I know that He blesses her efforts. I have seen the fruit of a mother’s patience. I know that Jesus Christ is the Master of every orchard. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to pick one small act of care to repeat daily, such as a bedtime blessing or a kind word at breakfast.

blessings: Love will become a habit at home.

closingVerse.text: And ye will not suffer your children that they go hungry, or naked; neither will ye suffer that they transgress the laws of God, and fight and quarrel one with another, and serve the devil, who is the master of sin, or who is the evil spirit which hath been spoken of by our fathers, he being an enemy to all righteousness. But ye will teach them to walk in the ways of truth and soberness; ye will teach them to love one another, and to serve one another.

opening.text: Think of a path across a field. Nobody built it. It was made by feet, walking the same way day after day. After a while, the grass stops growing there. The path is clear, and anyone can follow it.
A mother makes a path like that for her children. She walks it first, again and again, and her children learn the way.

mainMessage.text: Mothers show the way by walking it. They love, teach and pray, day after day. Over time, a clear path forms, and children know where to go.

blocks.text: **The first footsteps.** Someone had to walk the path first. God gave mothers that role from the beginning. It is part of His design.

For behold, this is my work and my glory—to bring to pass the immortality and eternal life of man.

**Wear it in early.** A path worn in the first season lasts. A habit taught in childhood lasts, too. Start while the child is small, and do not give up.
Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
President Gordon B. Hinckley, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Your Greatest Challenge, Mother” from the October 2000 general conference (General Women’s Meeting).
Teach your children when they are very young and small, and never quit.
A path worn early lasts.
**Worth the walking.** Walking the path takes effort. Teaching at home takes effort too. But it is among the most sacred things parents do.

Elder L. Tom Perry, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Mothers Teaching Children in the Home” from the April 2010 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).

The walking is sacred work.
**A rest stop.** Along every long path, there are places to stop and rest. For a mother, prayer is that place. It restores her strength.
Pray in your families unto the Father, always in my name, that your wives and your children may be blessed.

Prayer is where she rests.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they learned something by watching how their mother lived. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Mary Ponders in Her Heart

blocks.text: Mary was the mother of the Savior. She did not understand everything she saw. But she paid attention, and she kept it close.
But Mary kept all these things, and pondered them in her heart.
A mother who ponders and treasures can guide her children well.

application.text: First, think of a habit you want your children to learn. Ask yourself whether you show it first.
Second, take one step this week to live that habit in front of them.
Third, if you wish to talk about a family concern, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that mothers shape lives by how they live. I know that God honors their steady steps. I have seen the path a good mother makes. I know that Jesus Christ walks beside all who follow Him. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to think of a habit you want your children to learn.
I invite you to live that habit in front of them this week.
I invite you to speak with your bishop or branch president about any family concern.
blessings: Your children will learn by watching you.
You will grow in faith too.

closingVerse.text: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.

opening.text: In many families, there is a recipe that has no paper copy. It lives in someone’s hands. A grandmother knew it by feel. She showed her daughter how much, how long and when it was ready. Then the daughter showed her own children.
That is how many of the best things are passed on. Not by a manual, but by someone showing us, patiently, over and over.

mainMessage.text: Mothers pass on faith the way recipes are passed on. They show it, they say it, and they do it with love. God helps them, and what they give lasts for generations.

blocks.text: **An old, good recipe.** This way of passing things on is not new. God designed it. Mothers have been teaching the next generation since the first woman.
And Adam called his wife’s name Eve; because she was the mother of all living.
Elder L. Tom Perry, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Mothers Teaching Children in the Home” from the April 2010 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).

The recipe is old and good.
**Who it is for.** A family recipe is made for the people at the table. A mother’s love is poured into her children. They are the most precious people she knows.
And whoso shall receive one such little child in my name receiveth me.
President Gordon B. Hinckley, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Your Greatest Challenge, Mother” from the October 2000 general conference (General Women’s Meeting).
You have nothing in this world more precious than your children.
It is made for those she loves.

For behold, this is my work and my glory—to bring to pass the immortality and eternal life of man.

You have entered into a partnership with our Father in Heaven to give mortal experience to His sons and daughters.

**Teach it young.** Children who learn to cook beside a parent keep that skill for life. In the same way, what we teach early stays. Start young, and keep going.

Teach your children when they are very young and small, and never quit.
What we learn young, we keep.
**Show it, not just say it.** You cannot learn a recipe from a description alone. You need to watch and try. A mother teaches best when children see her live what she says.

Now they never had fought, yet they did not fear death; and they did think more upon the liberty of their fathers than they did upon their lives; yea, they had been taught by their mothers, that if they did not doubt, God would deliver them.
And they rehearsed unto me the words of their mothers, saying: We do not doubt our mothers knew it.
Elder L. Tom Perry, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Mothers Teaching Children in the Home” from the April 2010 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when a mother or grandmother taught them something that stayed with them. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Jochebed Nurses Her Own Child

blocks.text: Jochebed hid her baby son to keep him safe. In time, she was able to care for him in Pharaoh’s own house, and she taught him while he was young.
And Pharaoh’s daughter said unto her, Take this child away, and nurse it for me, and I will give thee thy wages. And the woman took the child, and nursed it.
A mother’s early care can shape a child who later leads many.

application.text: First, choose one thing you want your children to carry forward, such as a prayer, a hymn or a family saying.
Second, do it together this week, and tell them why it matters to you.
Third, if you feel unsure about what to pass on, speak with your bishop or branch president.

closingVerse.text: Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations: ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee.

opening.text: When a storm comes, a ship drops its anchor. The anchor does not stop the wind. It does not calm the waves. But it holds the ship in place. The crew can ride out the night and still be where they started when the morning comes.
A faithful mother is often an anchor for her family. The storms still come, but she holds steady.

mainMessage.text: Mothers hold families steady through faith, teaching and prayer. They are not alone in this work. God is their partner, and He holds them as they hold their children.

blocks.text: **Forged on purpose.** An anchor is made for one job. God made motherhood for a sacred purpose. It is part of His plan.
And Adam called his wife’s name Eve; because she was the mother of all living.
Elder L. Tom Perry, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Mothers Teaching Children in the Home” from the April 2010 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
I believe it is by divine design that the role of motherhood emphasizes the nurturing and teaching of the next generation.
The anchor has a purpose.
**What it holds.** The anchor holds the ship, and the ship carries everything the crew values. A mother holds on to her children, and nothing is more precious to her.
And whoso shall receive one such little child in my name receiveth me.
President Gordon B. Hinckley, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Your Greatest Challenge, Mother” from the October 2000 general conference (General Women’s Meeting).
You have nothing in this world more precious than your children.
She holds what matters most.
**Anchored to something firm.** An anchor works only when it grips the seabed. A mother’s strength comes from God. He is her partner, and she holds to Him.
For behold, this is my work and my glory—to bring to pass the immortality and eternal life of man.
President Gordon B. Hinckley, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Your Greatest Challenge, Mother” from the October 2000 general conference (General Women’s Meeting).
You have entered into a partnership with our Father in Heaven to give mortal experience to His sons and daughters.
She is anchored to Him.
**Set it before the storm.** A wise sailor drops the anchor early. A wise mother teaches early, before the storms of the teenage years. Start now, and do not stop.
Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
President Gordon B. Hinckley, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Your Greatest Challenge, Mother” from the October 2000 general conference (General Women’s Meeting).
Teach your children when they are very young and small, and never quit.
We set the anchor early.
**The weight of it.** An anchor is heavy, but that weight is what makes it work. The teaching a mother does at home is weighty too. It is among the most sacred things she can do.

Now they never had fought, yet they did not fear death; and they did think more upon the liberty of their fathers than they did upon their lives; yea, they had been taught by their mothers, that if they did not doubt, God would deliver them.
And they rehearsed unto me the words of their mothers, saying: We do not doubt our mothers knew it.

**The line to the ship.** The anchor is tied to the ship by a strong line. Prayer is the line that ties a mother to God. If she lets it go, she drifts. If she holds it, she is steady.

Prayer is the line that holds.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when a mother’s faith held a family steady in a storm. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The Mothers of the Stripling Warriors

blocks.text: The young soldiers of Helaman faced real danger. Their courage came from what their mothers had taught them.

Yea, and they did obey and observe to perform every word of command with exactness; yea, and even according to their faith it was done unto them; and I did remember the words which they said unto me that their mothers had taught them.
Their mothers were not on the battlefield. But what they taught went with their sons.

application.text: First, think of one truth you want your children to hold on to in hard times. Write it down.
Second, say it to them this week, in your own words.
Third, if you or a child is going through a storm, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that mothers who love God are a blessing to their families. I know that He supports them in their hardest days. I have seen a mother’s faith carry a family through a storm. I know that Jesus Christ is the Anchor of every soul. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to write down one truth you want your children to hold on to in hard times.

You will feel the Savior's help.
